title: Vulnerable groups and disinformation. An analysis of the Andalusian reality
screen_reason: Representative survey of 1,550 Andalusians aged 15+ (December 2023, Cotesa). Reports the share of respondents agreeing they often come across news or information they believe distorts reality or is false (87.9%), a self-reported exposure share, plus the share who perceive that traditional media (60%) and social media (79.2%) generate a lot or quite a lot of disinformation, which the protocol counts as perceived amount of misinformation in one's environment.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents agreeing (completely or somewhat) that they often come across news or information they believe distorts reality or is false
estimates.value_raw: 87,9% (42,9% completamente de acuerdo + 45,0% de acuerdo), stated as 87.9% in the text
estimates.denominator: 1,550 Andalusian residents aged 15 and over, quota sample stratified by habitat size with sex and age quotas (1,250 online, 300 by telephone among the 60+)
estimates.definition: Respondent answered 'completely agree' or 'agree' to the statement 'A menudo encuentra noticias o información que creen que distorsionan la realidad o incluso que son falsas' ('You often come across news or information that you believe distorts reality or is even false')
estimates.misinfo_def: "La desinformación es un fenómeno complejo y multifacético caracterizado por la difusión intencional de información falsa o engañosa, con el objetivo de causar daño o manipular la opinión pública" ("Disinformation is a complex, multifaceted phenomenon characterised by the intentional spread of false or misleading information, with the aim of causing harm or manipulating public opinion")
estimates.source_quote: Con respecto al grado de acuerdo con la frase de que a menudo se encuentran noticias falsas, existe un consenso general: el 87,9% de los andaluces confirma esta realidad (Tabla 3).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report on a four-point Likert agreement scale (completely agree / rather agree / rather disagree / completely disagree, plus don't know); items adapted from Eurobarometer and CIS instruments and pilot-tested with about twenty people
estimates.moderator_quote: Para cada una de las siguientes afirmaciones, ¿puede decir su grado de acuerdo o de desacuerdo?
estimates.notes: Sampling error reported as ±2.55% at 95.5% confidence for the whole sample. The item has no time window ('a menudo' / 'often'), so the exposure period is undefined.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who think social media generate a lot or quite a lot of disinformation
estimates.definition: Respondent answered 'mucha' or 'bastante' to how much disinformation is generated by social media
estimates.misinfo_def: "La desinformación es un fenómeno complejo y multifacético caracterizado por la difusión intencional de información falsa o engañosa" ("Disinformation is a complex, multifaceted phenomenon characterised by the intentional spread of false or misleading information")
estimates.source_quote: Por lo que se refiere a la responsabilidad de las redes sociales en la generación de desinformación (Tabla 6), existe consenso en que generan mucha o bastante desinformación (79,2%).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report on a four-point scale (mucha / bastante / poca / ninguna, plus don't know) asked of each actor
estimates.moderator_quote: De los siguientes actores, dígame si en su opinión en cada uno de ellos se genera mucha, bastante, poca o ninguna desinformación.
estimates.notes: Borderline: this is a perception of how much disinformation a class of sources generates, not of how much the respondent personally encountered. Kept because the protocol counts 'perceived amount of misinformation in one's environment (a lot / some / none)'. The 79.2% total is stated verbatim in the body text; the abstract rounds it to 80%.

estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who think conventional mass media generate a lot or quite a lot of disinformation
estimates.value_raw: 60% as stated in the abstract; Table 5 gives 17,7% 'mucha' and 43,0% 'bastante', described in the text as 'algo más de seis de cada diez'
estimates.definition: Respondent answered 'mucha' or 'bastante' to how much disinformation is generated by conventional mass media
estimates.misinfo_def: "La desinformación es un fenómeno complejo y multifacético caracterizado por la difusión intencional de información falsa o engañosa" ("Disinformation is a complex, multifaceted phenomenon characterised by the intentional spread of false or misleading information")
estimates.source_quote: traditional media are also seen as bearing responsibility (60%).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report on a four-point scale (mucha / bastante / poca / ninguna, plus don't know) asked of each actor
estimates.moderator_quote: Con respecto al papel que desempeñan los medios de comunicación (Tabla 5), los resultados muestran que algo más de seis de cada diez andaluces creen que generan mucha o bastante desinformación.
estimates.notes: Only the rounded 60% is stated verbatim (abstract); the exact total would be a cross-category sum of Table 5 (17.7 + 43.0 = 60.7), which R8 forbids computing, so the verbatim 60% is used. Same borderline status as the social-media row.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: the share who find it easy to identify false information (67.4% overall; 62.4% among 15-24s; 70.4% low education; 72.5% university; 70.8% high income) - this is perceived detection ability, not exposure, and belief/discernment measures are out of scope. Media-use shares (television 82.1%, radio 58.3%, social media 50.4%, digital press 36.7%, print press 14.7% at least weekly) are news consumption, not misinformation exposure. All sociodemographic subgroup breakdowns of the three extracted items (by sex, age, education, income) were left out per the rule to keep the headline figure; e.g. for 'often encounters false information': men 88.9% vs women 87%, university 91.4%, primary or less 90.8%. No estimate of actual (as opposed to perceived) misinformation exposure is reported anywhere in the paper.

rob.design: Cross-sectional survey by the polling firm Cotesa, December 2023, representative of the Andalusian population aged 15+; 1,250 online interviews plus 300 telephone interviews among people aged 60+ drawn from a panel of more than 9,000; stratified by habitat size with sex and age quotas from the 2021 Padrón Continuo and 2021 Census; sampling error ±2.55% at 95.5% confidence. No response rate reported. Items adapted from Eurobarometer and CIS surveys, pilot-tested with about twenty people. Analysis is descriptive with chi-square tests at alpha .05; income has 15% missing (NS/NC), dropped from cross-tabulations.
rob.item6_quote: A menudo encuentra noticias o información que creen que distorsionan la realidad o incluso que son falsas
rob.item10_quote: Con respecto al grado de acuerdo con la frase de que a menudo se encuentran noticias falsas, existe un consenso general: el 87,9% de los andaluces confirma esta realidad (Tabla 3).
